monologue: The card hums warm and quiet under my attention, a steady warmth that feels like a blanket. The Wide Anchor sits heavy there, pressing down on a wedge that seems too tired to matter. I reach out and touch the anchor's edge, feeling its rough scrap bite into the slippery base. It feels heavier than a stone, anchoring the slip against an air that might be empty or a lid, I cannot tell. I set a flat rock beside it, taking away a tired pillar to make room for the new weight. Now I wait, feeling the stack grow hot again, wondering if the lean I trusted will hold while the card boils. I want to see if the air above really presses down or if I am just dreaming of a roof I cannot see.

action.why: The anchor feels heavy and the stack is hot again; I must press down before the slip decides to slide into the empty air.
